name: The Governed Light
description: The earliest neural-feed film widely considered a genuine artistic landmark, produced in the medium's chaotic first years before Vantablack Media established licensing standards. Director-architect Yusuf Mwangi-Hesse structured the film as a recursive loop — the viewer experiences the same ninety-minute sequence six times, each repetition stripping away one layer of the protagonist's constructed identity until only raw sensory data remains. Contemporary audiences found it maddening; twenty years later it is cited by nearly every serious neural-feed filmmaker as a foundational influence.
cultural_impact: Established that neural-feed cinema could function as genuine philosophical inquiry rather than entertainment delivery, legitimizing the entire art-house immersion movement that followed.
story_hooks: Mwangi-Hesse died before the film was licensed and the original feed architecture has been slowly degrading — someone needs to recover and preserve it before it corrupts entirely.
A Tier 4 collector claims to own the only complete first-generation copy and is using it to exert influence over the art-house community in ways that are becoming coercive.
A researcher studying the film's recursive structure believes Mwangi-Hesse encoded a message in the degradation pattern of the sixth loop — one that becomes legible only as the file decays.
